# #2994: CI: daily super run failed
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[super run 41771700184](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41771700184) on `main` (`620d660`, workflow_dispatch) failed:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| [e2e component (chrome)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41771700184/job/126385726319) | failure |

Each link opens that job's log. This issue stays open while the run is red and the next run that passes every job closes it. `gh workflow run super.yml --ref <branch>` runs it again on demand.

Night bot: this run is on `main`, so it is yours, and it comes first (`priority:high`): production promotes itself only from a run on `main` that passes every job, so it waits on this fix. Root-cause each failed job from its log and fix it in a pull request: a flake is not a root cause, so make a flaky test robust instead of re-running it, and never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get green. Reproduce it with the job's own command (CLAUDE.md, Commands; one fuzz seed is `cargo jackioh fuzz --from <seed> --seeds 1`, with `--handicap` for the handicapped wave and `--duos` for the Duos wave; a daily test is `cargo test -p <crate> <name> -- --ignored`). A pull request's CI runs only the e2e smoke specs and leaves the tests marked `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` out, so say in the pull request which job here the fix makes pass and how you checked it. You cannot change `.github/`: make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, and when the rest needs a workflow or an action, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/super.yml`._
